plot: The morning after Turbo's try-out, Bertha arrives at school at eight to find no kids at the stops or the school; Benny's bakery is still shut, the street lamps are still on, Grumpy and Pip insist it's seven, and the kids are found asleep in pyjamas; Bolt finally remembers the note the wind blew away: the clocks went back one hour last night, so it is the 'eight o'clock' cars who are an hour early, and Bolt says sorry for not sharing the clue; they spend the extra hour watching the sunrise with Benny's free rolls and pick the kids up right on time; lesson: when something looks strange, check the simple things first; cliffhanger: Hal will sell his grandma's apples at market day from his moving truck.

script.title: Why Is the School Empty?!
script.description: Thirty kids are missing from school... or are they? Inspector Bolt #25

set.place: Wheelburg school gate, Benny's bakery, Grumpy's tow yard and Gear Street, Wednesday at dawn

beats.say: Eight o'clock! School time! Honk, honk! Good morning, kids!
Kids? Hello? Where IS everybody?
No kids at the bus stops. No kids at school. Not one!
It was Wednesday morning, the day after Turbo's big try-out.
And the sun was only just peeking over the hills.
Good morning, Bertha. Eight o'clock sharp, as always.
Sharp, yes! But where are my thirty kids?
Thirty kids, nowhere to be seen? Then this is a case.
Just then, Hal rolled by, stretching and smiling.
Morning! What a lovely long sleep. Like I got an extra hour!
Hal! Have you seen any kids this morning?
Kids? Not yet. Only one very sleepy bird.
Anyway, I'm off to paint something special. Bye!
Let us start where the kids start. The bakery.
Every school morning, the kids buy warm rolls at Benny's bakery.
But this morning, the bakery door was shut tight.
Shut? Benny never shuts on a school day!
I'm here! Still baking! The shop opens at eight.
But Benny, it IS eight! Look at my clock!
Is it? My oven clock says five past seven.
Oh, poor Benny. Your clock is broken, dear.
Broken? It's a brand new clock. Hmm. Strange.
Bolt didn't say a word. He looked up at the sky.
The sun is very low for eight o'clock.
Never mind the sun, Bolt! My kids are nowhere!
Morning, team! I'm at my crossing at eight, like always!
But nobody wants to cross! Not even one kid!
If we don't find them, there's no school today!
No school? But today is painting day! They love painting day!
Then Bolt noticed something odd. The street lamps were still on.
The lamps switch off at half past seven. Every day.
So why are they still shining at eight?
Maybe the lamps overslept too?
Lamps don't oversleep, Turbo. Let's ask someone who knows lamps.
So they rolled to Grumpy's tow yard. Grumpy was fast asleep.
Zzz... Go away. It's seven. I have one more hour.
Seven? Grumpy, it's eight! Your clock is broken too!
My clock is fine. You're the one who's broken.
Then a tiny pink car rolled out of her garage, yawning.
Why is everyone up so early? It's only seven.
Benny says seven. Grumpy says seven. Pip says seven.
Bertha says eight. Turbo says eight. My clock says eight.
So half of Wheelburg is broken? Which half?
Not our half! We're the ones who are always on time!
Then let's look in a house! Are the kids even there?
They rolled quietly to the yellow house on Gear Street.
Pip peeked through the window. Two kids were fast asleep.
They're in pyjamas! They're still sleeping!
On a school day? Who sleeps until eight on a school day?
The bell rings at half past eight! They'll all be late!
Should I honk? A tiny honk? A medium honk?
Wait. No honking. Something doesn't fit.
Bolt thought about the lamps. The bakery. The sleepy kids.
And then about a little note, flying away in the wind.
The note on the town hall door. Last night. Oh dear.
It said, 'Tonight the clocks go back one hour.'
Our clocks say eight. But the real time is seven.
So the kids aren't late... we are one hour EARLY!
So the lamps, the bakery, Grumpy... they were all right?
Told you. My clock is fine.
I'm afraid this is my fault. I read the note and forgot.
I'm sorry, everyone. A good detective shares his clues.
Oh, Bolt. Everybody forgets sometimes. Even detectives.
So we have a whole extra hour? What do we do with it?
Something we never have time for! Come on, everyone!
So they parked in a row on the hill and watched the sunrise.
Warm rolls for the early birds! The first ones are free!
Best mistake ever! Can the clocks go back every day?
At eight o'clock, the real eight o'clock, the kids came running.
Good morning, my darlings! All aboard! We're right on time!
When something looks strange, check the simple things first.
Like the clock!
Look, everyone! I used my extra hour to paint a sign!
Tomorrow is market day. I'm selling my grandma's apples!
Apples? From a big moving truck?
Hmm. Who buys apples from a moving truck?
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
